brief: GS Morning covers five items. On the Trump-Xi summit, Bessent confirmed a two-month trade-truce extension while Chinese state media reported Xi pushing the US toward an explicit oppose-Taiwan-independence stance versus the current do-not-support formulation, plus AI-dialogue and Iran-mediation talk. GS calls it not yet market-moving and flags Iran as the item to watch. Banxico held its rate at 6.50% unanimously, matching consensus, but GS thinks its 2026/27 inflation forecasts are too optimistic, with risk skewed toward higher inflation and slower growth, so GS's FX desk is tactically short USDMXN, with 17.80 as support and 18.00 as the psychological level. For Brazil's election, GS lists nine desk trade ideas across equities, options, rates, FX and credit, positioning for a Lula-Bolsonaro race that has tightened into a near-toss-up runoff. On AI capex, hyperscalers are on pace for $800bn in 2026 spend, and GS expects capex to beat 2027 consensus even as growth decelerates, while estimating hyperscalers need about $300bn in annual AI revenue to break even. On PMIs, GS argues the September flash-PMI-driven Treasury selloff was an overreaction, partly nominal-bias inflated, and keeps its 2.2% 2026 GDP forecast.
